title: Canonical identification of a supported triangle by its first arrow
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $A$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with exact $i_*$ and $i^*,j^*$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $i^!_0M=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], and write $S=Ri^!_0$ on $D^+$, with its support counit $\epsilon:i_*SK\to K$ as in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. Suppose given a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$i_*L\xrightarrow{a}K\xrightarrow{\eta_j}Rj_*j^*K\xrightarrow{b}(i_*L)[1],$$
whose second arrow is the open adjunction unit. Let
$$\theta:L\longrightarrow SK,\qquad \epsilon_K\circ i_*\theta=a,$$
be the unique transpose of $a$ under $i_*\dashv S$. Then $\theta$ is an isomorphism, and $(i_*\theta,\operatorname{id}_K,\operatorname{id}_{Rj_*j^*K})$ is an isomorphism from the given triangle to the support-localization triangle of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle], including its third arrow. This isomorphism is independent of any completion of a morphism of triangles. For families of such triangles in which $a$ is natural, $\theta$ is natural. No etale-origin or constructibility hypothesis on $K,L$ is imposed.

source.place: Canonical identification of the supported first term and boundary (old item Steps 4--5)

proof.text: First obtain full faithfulness of the termwise derived $i_*$. The inverse-image/direct-image adjunction and exactness of $i^*$ are supplied by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; $i_*$ is exact under the hypotheses of the statement. The sheaf counit $i^*i_*\to1$ is invertible by [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful], for the finite constant ring $A$ and without constructibility. Apply [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction] to these two exact additive functors. Its derived counit is the localized degreewise counit, hence invertible: its inverse is obtained by applying localization to the degreewise inverse. The functors preserve bounded below complexes termwise, so restrict to $D^+$. In the resulting adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$ the Hom bijection followed by precomposition with the invertible counit gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*L,i_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(L,M)$, inverse to applying $i_*$. Thus $i_*$ is fully faithful on $D^+$.

source.place: Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion) and 09BM (lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact); exact adjunction localized as specified by def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction

proof.text:
Write $C=Rj_*j^*K$ and let $\delta:C\to(i_*SK)[1]$ be the boundary in the specified support triangle. By [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] that triangle is distinguished and its first arrow is the support counit of $i_*\dashv S$. Combining the full faithfulness proved in step 1 with this adjunction gives the bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*L,i_*SK)\xrightarrow{\ \epsilon_K\circ-\ }\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*L,K).$$
Indeed the first Hom set is identified with $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(L,SK)$ by $i_*$, and the inverse-transpose formula is $u\mapsto\epsilon_K\circ i_*u$. Consequently any $c:i_*L\to i_*SK$ with $\epsilon_Kc=a$ must equal $i_*\theta$.

source.place: Agent argument using the support adjunction; compare Tag 0145, TR3, for the next step

proof.text:
Rotate both distinguished triangles once, using TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Their first arrows are the same $\eta_j:K\to C$. Apply TR3 to the identity maps of $K$ and $C$; obtain $t:(i_*L)[1]\to(i_*SK)[1]$ such that
$$t\circ b=\delta,\qquad (-\epsilon_K[1])\circ t=-a[1].$$
Since shift is an additive autoequivalence, there is a unique $c:i_*L\to i_*SK$ with $c[1]=t$ (under its canonical inverse-shift identifications). Cancelling the minus signs and using faithfulness of shift gives $\epsilon_Kc=a$. The other equation gives $c[1]b=\delta$. Thus $(c,1_K,1_C)$ is a morphism of the unrotated triangles, including the boundary square. By step 2, $c=i_*\theta$.

source.place: Tag 0145 (definition-triangulated-category), TR2 and TR3, with the signed rotation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to the morphism of distinguished triangles of step 3: its middle and third components are identities, so $i_*\theta$ is invertible. Full faithfulness from step 1 reflects this isomorphism explicitly: lift $(i_*\theta)^{-1}$ to $v:SK\to L$; faithfulness applied to the two inverse equations gives $v\theta=1_L$ and $\theta v=1_{SK}$. Thus $\theta$ is invertible. By [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], componentwise invertibility of $(i_*\theta,1_K,1_C)$ makes it an isomorphism in the category of triangles. Its last square is the equation $(i_*\theta)[1]b=\delta$ already proved, so the prescribed third arrow is respected.

Every completion in step 3 has first component $c$ satisfying $\epsilon_Kc=a$, so step 2 forces the same $i_*\theta$. The other components are fixed identities. Hence the isomorphism is independent of the completion. For natural families on this fixed closed-open pair, let $u:L\to L'$ and $v:K\to K'$ satisfy $v a=a'i_*u$. The support adjunction and natural counit in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] give
$$\epsilon_{K'}\,i_*(S(v)\theta)=v\epsilon_K i_*\theta=va=a'i_*u=\epsilon_{K'}\,i_*(\theta'u).$$
The bijection of step 2, now with target $K'$, and faithfulness of $i_*$ give $S(v)\theta=\theta'u$. This proves the asserted naturality. All arguments used all ordinary finite constant-$A$ module sheaves and $D^+$; no etale-origin or constructibility restriction was introduced.
